falsifier: A triangle-free cover for which least-layer assignment creates a triangle.
novelty: "triangle-free edge cover" partition equivalence least layer
proof: The implications (2)\(\Leftrightarrow\)(3) are definitional. A partition is a cover, so (2)\(\Rightarrow\)(1). For (1)\(\Rightarrow\)(2), well-order the \(\lambda\) covering layers and assign each edge to the least layer containing it. Each new layer is a subgraph of an original triangle-free layer and is therefore triangle-free.
title: Cover–Partition Equivalence

falsifier: A family of at most κ edge sets, each κ-coverable, whose union is not κ-coverable.
proof: Downward closure follows because every subgraph of a triangle-free graph is triangle-free. Let \(\{F_i:i\in I\}\subseteq\mathcal I_\kappa(G)\) with \(|I|\le\kappa\). For each \(i\), cover \(F_i\) by at most \(\kappa\) triangle-free layers. All these layers together number at most \(|I|\cdot\kappa\le\kappa\), because \(\kappa\) is infinite. They cover \(\bigcup_iF_i\).
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be an infinite cardinal and \(G\) a graph. Define
\[
\mathcal I_\kappa(G)=
\{F\subseteq E(G): tc((V(G),F))\le \kappa\}.
\]
Then \(\mathcal I_\kappa(G)\) is downward closed and closed under unions of at most \(\kappa\) members.
title: The κ-Complete Triangle-Cover Ideal

falsifier: A graph of triangle-cover number above κ that becomes κ-coverable after deleting a κ-coverable edge set.
novelty: "triangle cover number" deletion persistence edge ideal
proof: If \(tc(G-F)\le\kappa\), then \(E(G)=F\cup E(G-F)\) is the union of two members of \(\mathcal I_\kappa(G)\). By T1 it belongs to \(\mathcal I_\kappa(G)\), contradicting \(tc(G)>\kappa\).
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite. If \(tc(G)>\kappa\) and \(F\in\mathcal I_\kappa(G)\), then
\[
tc(G-F)>\kappa.
\]
title: Null-Edge Deletion Persistence

falsifier: An edge-minimal graph with triangle-cover number above an infinite κ.
proof: A set of at most \(\kappa\) individual edges is covered by at most \(\kappa\) one-edge triangle-free layers. Apply T2.
statement: If \(\kappa\) is infinite and \(tc(G)>\kappa\), then deleting any single edge, any set of at most \(\kappa\) edges, or more generally any edge set of triangle-cover number at most \(\kappa\), leaves triangle-cover number greater than \(\kappa\). In particular, no such graph is edge-minimal for the property \(tc>\kappa\).
title: No Edge-Minimal High-Cover Graph

falsifier: A graph with tc>κ and a vertex set of size at most κ whose deletion makes tc≤κ.
proof: Let \(F_S\) be the set of all edges incident with at least one vertex of \(S\). It is covered by the \(|S|\) stars centered at vertices of \(S\), and every star is triangle-free. Hence \(F_S\in\mathcal I_\kappa(G)\). The spanning graph \(G-F_S\) is \(G-S\) together with isolated vertices from \(S\), so the two graphs have the same triangle-cover number. Apply T2.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite. If \(tc(G)>\kappa\) and \(S\subseteq V(G)\) has \(|S|\le\kappa\), then
\[
tc(G-S)>\kappa.
\]
title: Small-Vertex Deletion Persistence

falsifier: A disjoint union whose triangle-cover number differs from the supremum of those of its components.
proof: Restriction of any triangle-free cover of \(G\) to \(G_i\) proves \(tc(G_i)\le tc(G)\), giving the lower bound. For the upper bound, let \(\lambda=\sup_i tc(G_i)\). Color the edges of every component with the same palette \(\lambda\), using a nonmonochromatic-triangle coloring within that component. A triangle lies in one component, so the combined coloring is valid.
statement:
If \(G\) is the disjoint union of its connected components \(\{G_i:i\in I\}\), then
\[
tc(G)=\sup_{i\in I} tc(G_i).
\]
title: Component Supremum Formula

falsifier: A high-cover graph and small separator for which every residual component is κ-coverable.
proof: By T3, \(tc(G-S)>\kappa\). If every component of \(G-S\) had triangle-cover number at most \(\kappa\), T4 would imply \(tc(G-S)\le\kappa\), a contradiction.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite. If \(tc(G)>\kappa\) and \(|S|\le\kappa\), then some connected component \(C\) of \(G-S\) satisfies
\[
tc(C)>\kappa.
\]
title: Small-Separator Escape

falsifier: A well-ordered graph with all forward links κ-colorable but tc>κ.
novelty: "forward neighborhood" chromatic number triangle-free edge cover
proof:
For every \(v\), choose a proper vertex-coloring
\(\varphi_v:N_\prec^+(v)\to\kappa\). For an edge \(vw\) with \(v\prec w\), color \(vw\) by \(\varphi_v(w)\). Consider a triangle \(v\prec w\prec x\). The vertices \(w,x\) are adjacent inside \(G[N_\prec^+(v)]\), so \(\varphi_v(w)\ne\varphi_v(x)\). Thus the edges \(vw\) and \(vx\) have different colors, and the triangle is not monochromatic.
statement:
Let \(\prec\) be a well-order of \(V(G)\), and define
\[
N_\prec^+(v)=\{w\in N_G(v):v\prec w\}.
\]
If every forward link \(G[N_\prec^+(v)]\) is \(\kappa\)-colorable, then
\[
tc(G)\le\kappa.
\]
title: Ordered Forward-Link Coloring

falsifier: A K4-free graph of tc>κ with a well-order whose every forward link is κ-colorable.
proof: The chromatic conclusion is the contrapositive of T6. A triangle in \(N_G(v)\), together with \(v\), would form a \(K_4\); hence every full or forward link is triangle-free.
statement:
Let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free and let \(\kappa\) be a cardinal. If \(tc(G)>\kappa\), then for every well-order \(\prec\) of \(V(G)\), some vertex \(v\) satisfies
\[
\chi(G[N_\prec^+(v)])>\kappa,
\]
and this forward link is triangle-free.
title: High-Cover Link Extraction in \(K_4\)-Free Graphs

falsifier: A K4-free high-cover graph in which the recursion first fails at some ordinal below κ+.
novelty: "κ+ long" high chromatic neighborhood tower K4-free
proof:
Proceed by transfinite recursion. At stage \(\alpha<\kappa^+\), let
\(S_\alpha=\{v_\beta:\beta<\alpha\}\). Since \(\alpha<\kappa^+\), \(|S_\alpha|\le\kappa\). By T3, \(G-S_\alpha\) still has triangle-cover number greater than \(\kappa\). Choose any well-order of its vertices and apply T7 to obtain a new apex \(v_\alpha\) and a high-chromatic triangle-free forward link \(L_\alpha\) in the residual. The apex is new because it lies outside \(S_\alpha\).
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite and \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with \(tc(G)>\kappa\). Then there is a sequence
\[
\langle (v_\alpha,L_\alpha):\alpha<\kappa^+\rangle
\]
such that the vertices \(v_\alpha\) are distinct and every \(L_\alpha\) is an induced triangle-free subgraph of \(G\) with
\[
L_\alpha\subseteq N_G(v_\alpha)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\chi(L_\alpha)>\kappa.
\]
title: Successor-Length Forward-Link Tower

falsifier: A maximal triangle-free spanning subgraph with an omitted edge having no common H-neighbor, or with two adjacent certificate vertices.
novelty: "maximal triangle-free subgraph" omitted edge stable common neighbors
proof: Maximality of \(H\) implies that adding \(xy\) creates a triangle, so some \(z\) satisfies \(xz,yz\in E(H)\); hence \(W_H(xy)\ne\varnothing\). If distinct \(z,z'\in W_H(xy)\) were adjacent in \(G\), then \(x,y,z,z'\) would have all six edges: \(xy,zz'\in E(G)\), and the four cross-edges lie in \(H\). This is a \(K_4\), contradiction.
statement:
Let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free and \(H\) a maximal spanning triangle-free subgraph of \(G\). If \(xy\in E(G)\setminus E(H)\), define
\[
W_H(xy)=N_H(x)\cap N_H(y).
\]
Then \(W_H(xy)\) is nonempty and stable in \(G\).
title: Stable Certification of Omitted Edges

falsifier: At most κ maximal triangle-free layers with no common omitted edge, or a common omitted edge lacking a stable certificate in one layer.
novelty: "common omitted edge" maximal triangle-free layers stable book
proof: If no edge were omitted by all \(H_i\), then the edge sets \(E(H_i)\) would cover \(E(G)\), contradicting \(tc(G)>\kappa\). Choose a common omitted edge and apply T9 to each layer.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite, \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free, and \(tc(G)>\kappa\). For every family
\[
\{H_i:i\in I\}
\]
of maximal spanning triangle-free subgraphs with \(|I|\le\kappa\), there is an edge \(xy\in E(G)\) omitted by every \(H_i\). For each \(i\), \(W_{H_i}(xy)\) is a nonempty stable subset of \(N_G(x)\cap N_G(y)\).
title: Common Omitted-Edge Stable Book

falsifier: A nonempty stable book that is triangle-free or requires at least three triangle-free layers.
novelty: "stable triangle book" triangle cover number two
proof:
The graph contains a triangle \(xyw\), so its triangle-cover number is greater than one. It is covered by two triangle-free layers:
\[
\{xy\}\cup\{xw:w\in W\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\{yw:w\in W\}.
\]
The first is a star with one additional incident edge \(xy\), and the second is a star; neither contains a triangle.
statement:
Let \(x,y\) be adjacent and let \(W\subseteq N(x)\cap N(y)\) be a nonempty stable set. Let \(B(xy,W)\) be the graph with edge set
\[
\{xy\}\cup\{xw,yw:w\in W\}.
\]
Then
\[
tc(B(xy,W))=2.
\]
title: Stable Triangle-Book Sterility

falsifier: A #595-type graph that becomes countably triangle-decomposable after deleting countably many stable books.
novelty: "countably many stable books" triangle cover deletion persistence
proof: Each stable book has triangle-cover number two by T11. Their countable union has countable triangle-cover number by T1. Apply T2 with \(\kappa=\aleph_0\).
statement:
Let \(G\) be a \(K_4\)-free graph with \(tc(G)>\aleph_0\). If \(F\) is the union of the edge sets of countably many stable triangle books, then
\[
tc(G-F)>\aleph_0.
\]
title: Countable Book-Deletion Persistence

falsifier: A first stage below ω1 at which the countable deletion, link extraction, finite compactness, or induced-cone step fails.
novelty: "ω1 many disjoint induced cones" critical triangle-free graphs
proof: At stage \(\alpha<\omega_1\), fewer than \(\omega_1\) finite cones have been chosen, so their union of vertices is countable. Delete it; T3 leaves a \(K_4\)-free graph of uncountable triangle-cover number. By T7 it has an uncountably chromatic triangle-free link \(L\) at an apex \(v\). By the de Bruijn–Erdős compactness theorem for finite colorings, \(L\) has a finite induced subgraph of chromatic number greater than \(f(\alpha)\). Choose one minimal by vertex deletion and call it \(Q_\alpha\); it is vertex-critical. Since \(Q_\alpha\subseteq N(v)\), the vertices \(\{v\}\cup V(Q_\alpha)\) induce the cone \(K_1\vee Q_\alpha\). The prior deletion makes the cones pairwise vertex-disjoint.
statement:
Let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with \(tc(G)>\aleph_0\), and let
\(f:\omega_1\to\omega\). Then \(G\) contains pairwise vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs
\[
K_1\vee Q_\alpha\qquad(\alpha<\omega_1),
\]
where every \(Q_\alpha\) is finite, triangle-free, vertex-critical, and
\[
\chi(Q_\alpha)>f(\alpha).
\]
title: ω₁ Disjoint Critical-Cone Packing

falsifier: A verified #738(T) theorem and a #595-type graph in which the disjoint-cone recursion fails.
proof: Repeat the recursion in T13. After deleting the countable set of vertices used earlier, T3 and T7 produce an uncountably chromatic triangle-free link at a new apex. Apply the assumed Erdős #738 statement to find an induced \(T\) in that link, and adjoin the apex.
statement:
Fix a finite tree \(T\). Assume every triangle-free graph of infinite chromatic number contains an induced copy of \(T\). Then every \(K_4\)-free graph \(G\) with \(tc(G)>\aleph_0\) contains \(\omega_1\) pairwise vertex-disjoint induced copies of
\[
K_1\vee T.
\]
title: Conditional ω₁ Cone Packing from Erdős #738
